label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 14
knowledgePattern: Separate a guaranteed midpoint property from other equal-diagonal claims
solution:
Join the four side midpoints in order. In each of the original triangles, the line joining two midpoints is parallel to the third side and half its length, by similarity. The four new sides therefore alternate between half of AC and half of BD. Since the diagonals are equal, all four new sides are equal, so the midpoint quadrilateral is a rhombus. Statement I is true.

For the others, use the convex quadrilateral A=(0,0), B=(1,1), C=(5,0) and D=(4,−3). Its diagonals have lengths AC=5 and BD=32+42=5. The diagonals meet internally at (7/4,0), and the successive turns all have the same sign, so this is a valid convex quadrilateral.

The slopes of AB and CD are 1 and 3; those of BC and DA are −1/4 and −3/4. Neither pair of opposite sides is parallel, refuting II. The four side lengths squared are 2,17,10,25, all distinct. A reflection symmetry of a quadrilateral would pair at least two sides of equal length, so III is false.

Finally AB2+CD2=12 while BC2+DA2=42, refuting IV. Only I is guaranteed: answer A.

hints.title: Draw the diagonals first
hints.body: Draw two equal-length segments crossing away from their midpoints. Join their endpoints in order to make a convex quadrilateral.
hints.recap: Equal diagonals alone do not specify the positions of their intersection.
hints.pitfall: Keep the quadrilateral convex when trying examples.
hints.pause: Use this as a test diagram for the claims.

recall.reminder: Test a universal geometry claim with a proof or a valid counterexample.

hints.title: Use one triangle at a time
hints.body: Join the midpoints of two sides in one of the triangles formed by a diagonal. Use similarity to compare that small segment with the diagonal.
hints.recap: Two equal angle pairs establish triangle similarity and a common length scale.
hints.pitfall: Repeat the argument for all four midpoint sides.

hints.title: Check an irregular example
hints.body: Choose coordinates for an unequal-looking convex example with equal diagonals. Calculate its side lengths and gradients, then test the remaining claims.
hints.recap: One counterexample must satisfy every stated assumption.
hints.pitfall: A rectangle verifies only that special example.
hints.pause: Decide which remaining statements always hold.
